flavour.codex.exit.three-cards: The Exit cashes in small on purpose. Three nodes out of a tech tree of about a hundred and twenty, one Doctrine, the Playbook: three cards chosen on a screen, with everything else visibly filed away. Which memories to keep is the entire meta-progression. The filing away is the pain.
flavour.codex.exit.handwriting: The next company opens its first chapter on a whiteboard that already carries three cards, and the handwriting on them is the previous company's. Nobody explains it to the new hires. The run remembers.
flavour.codex.exit.ipo.headline: The bell rings, and the number on the tape is larger than every invoice the company ever sent. The building still runs on call rotations; the calendar now runs the call rotations.
flavour.codex.exit.ipo.body1: The filings read your churn curve back to the whole market. What the last twelve months were really for is now two hundred pages of proof that the boring decisions were the strategy all along.
flavour.codex.exit.ipo.body2: Five years on, the company still ships; it ships to the earnings calendar now. The quarterly target you cashed out for is the quarter you can never stop making, on this run and on every run the save keeps playing.
flavour.codex.exit.ipo.body3: The camera pulls back through the building and out to the world: every light on, your mark intact, and the hold lasts much longer than is comfortable. A public company is an institution that has forgotten how to blink.
flavour.codex.exit.ipo.profile: Most currency of any exit, paid once, plus a permanent modifier no later round can sell away: shareholder pressure — quarterly profit targets on all future runs.
flavour.codex.exit.strategic-acquisition.headlin: A bigger host buys the customer list and the rack space in the same sentence. The logo comes down the same week the multiple goes up in the trade press.
flavour.codex.exit.strategic-acquisition.body1: The customers wake up on a larger machine wearing your name like a borrowed coat. Nothing breaks, which is the best version of this ending: the uptime was real, and it is now filed under someone else.
flavour.codex.exit.strategic-acquisition.body2: The integration changelog lists your datacenter as a completed task. The staff list gets shorter in the quiet way org charts do when somebody else is writing them; most of the people who built this were not part of the price.
flavour.codex.exit.strategic-acquisition.body3: One postscript level remains after the close: you, on the acquirer's side of the table, cutting costs at a company you just bought — its staff, its customers, its history, all of it shown in the same detail the game once showed you yours. Ten minutes, no combat, quietly devastating.
flavour.codex.exit.strategic-acquisition.profile: Highest multiple on the table, and the only currency that spends itself: the brand dies at closing, most of the staff follows it out, and what the next run keeps is the check, not the company.
flavour.codex.exit.pe-platform.headline: They did not buy you to fold you in. They bought you to be the floor the next eleven acquisitions stand on, and handed you the keys: you stay, you run it, you are the platform now.
flavour.codex.exit.pe-platform.body1: Margin pressure arrives wearing your own management style: the same faces, the thinner spreads, and a board deck that prints your gross margin every quarter whether there is news or not.
flavour.codex.exit.pe-platform.body2: Year three, the roll-up has a shape and your onboarding runbook is its playbook. Year five, the second bite at the apple arrives: somebody is modelling your exit the way you once modelled an acquisition, and this time the multiple compounds on you.
flavour.codex.exit.pe-platform.body3: Five years on, the racks you racked are still up and the ones they bolted on are already depreciated in somebody's model. The camera holds on a building that is yours and is not yours, and does not resolve the sentence.
flavour.codex.exit.pe-platform.profile: A platform's payout: a mid multiple that pays in two bites five years apart. You keep the company and the seat; from closing, the margin line keeps you.
flavour.codex.exit.pe-bolt-on.headline: You were not a platform; you were a feature of one. The migration notice goes out under their brand, in your customers' own language, inside the week.
flavour.codex.exit.pe-bolt-on.body1: The cutover is fast because it is rehearsed. Your status page stops updating the way a heart stops between beats: not with an outage, with a redirect.
flavour.codex.exit.pe-bolt-on.body2: High churn is the line item the model already knew about. Customers renew onto their stack without ceremony, and the ones who never renew were never really yours — they were the box they lived on.
flavour.codex.exit.pe-bolt-on.body3: Five years on, your incidents open tickets on someone else's ladder and the customers' new hires have never heard the name. The pullback shot passes your building twice: once as yours, once as theirs, same lights.
flavour.codex.exit.pe-bolt-on.profile: The lower multiple, paid fast. The customers move onto the buyer's stack on the buyer's clock, the churn curve finishes the farewell, and the next run inherits a migration scar for every box that did not make it.
flavour.codex.exit.asset-sale.headline: They bought the book, not the company. The purchase agreement contained two lists; the money is on one of them, and everything else is on yours.
flavour.codex.exit.asset-sale.body1: What transfers is the customer ledger. What stays is the domain invoices, the last router's lease, a support contract from a decade ago nobody terminated on purpose, and a non-compete that locks you out of the segment you just sold for three years.
flavour.codex.exit.asset-sale.body2: For nine months you run their platform for them under a transition agreement, with your remaining staff, for a fee that reads generous until payroll is subtracted. The line you sold is still warm in your hands when the term ends.
flavour.codex.exit.asset-sale.body3: Five years on, the entity that once owned the company files a return with almost nothing in it, and the customers are content two brands over. The epilogue is short; the shell reads it as long.
flavour.codex.exit.asset-sale.profile: Cash for the book, liability for the shell. The multiple is real money moving onto real paper, and everything that was heavy stays exactly where you are standing.
flavour.codex.exit.management-buyout.headline: The signatures on the note are the same hands that racked the servers. The paper changes owners; the runbook does not change at all.
flavour.codex.exit.management-buyout.body1: Nobody notices the exit from the customer side: same tickets, same faces, same three nines. The only visible change is that the escalation path now terminates in people who answer the pager themselves.
flavour.codex.exit.management-buyout.body2: The equity pool is the staff list. Everyone who stayed now owns the box they have been babysitting, at the lowest price the bank would write and the only price that ever felt fair.
flavour.codex.exit.management-buyout.body3: Five years on, the Days Since Last Outage counter is still climbing after the credits of your own last working day. The unique perk this exit unlocks is not drawn on any tree: the company outlives the founder's absence without an acquirer doing it.
flavour.codex.exit.management-buyout.profile: Lowest cash of any exit, highest continuity of any ending, and the only close that opens the unique door on the perk tree. The currency here is measured in people who are still answering tickets in year five.
flavour.codex.exit.wind-down.headline: The last invoice pays the last vendor. What is left after the creditors is yours, and enough of it to keep the words: an available, dignified ending.
flavour.codex.exit.wind-down.body1: The book sells at a discount nobody apologizes for and the hardware goes to a refurbisher. The migration notices are written in your own words: every customer gets a date, a plan, and a forwarding address for their data.
flavour.codex.exit.wind-down.body2: The racks come down in dependency order, each one only after every customer on it has moved. When the last light goes out it is the exit sign, and this time it is pointing you out on your own schedule.
flavour.codex.exit.wind-down.body3: Five years on, no incident anywhere files under your name, and that silence is the record. The obituary nobody has to write turns out to be the one worth reading.
flavour.codex.exit.wind-down.profile: The exit that pays in time. The book goes, the hardware goes, the creditors get paid first, and what remains — the remainder, the clean ledger, the name without an asterisk — is the meta-currency of the next company's first page.
